video_caption: The video begins with a red equal sign centered on a plain gray background. This quickly transitions to a white background where the equal sign transforms: the top bar becomes blue on the left and red on the right, resembling a stylized American flag, while the bottom bar remains solid red. Below this symbol, the text "FIX DEMOCRACY" appears, followed by a red line and "FIRST" in red. Subsequently, "LESSIG 2016" is displayed above the flag-like symbol, and "lessig2016.us" appears in the top right corner. The scene then fades to a medium shot of a man, Lawrence Lessig, with short gray hair and glasses, wearing a light blue striped button-down shirt. He speaks earnestly, looking slightly off-camera against a soft, warm brown background. The "lessig2016.us" website remains visible in the top right. A brief cut shows Lessig, now in a black button-down shirt and black pants, walking across a stage, gesturing with his hands, in front of a large, seated audience in an auditorium. He then returns to the previous medium shot, continuing to speak with an engaged expression.

The video features a man with short gray hair and glasses. Initially, he is seen in a wide shot on a stage, speaking into a microphone stand to a seated audience, wearing a dark blue long-sleeved shirt. Behind him, a large screen displays the text "[(re)creativity]", and two vertical screens on either side show portraits. The stage is illuminated with red lights, creating a dynamic background. The scene then transitions to a close-up of the man, still on stage, gesturing with a closed fist as he speaks, maintaining a focused expression. This is followed by a distinct cut to a new setting where the man, now wearing a light blue striped button-up shirt, is in a dimly lit room with a plain brown background, speaking directly to the camera and using expressive hand gestures. Throughout the entire video, the text "LESSIG 2016" and "lessig2016.us" (no translation needed as it's a name and website) is visible as a watermark, subtly repeating around the frame.

The video opens with an exterior shot of the US Capitol Building, featuring the American flag waving against a clear blue sky, with the text "lessig2016.us" appearing in the top right corner (which means "lessig2016.us" as a website address). This transitions to a medium shot of an older man with white hair and glasses, wearing a brown suit and a yellow tie, speaking in what appears to be a studio setting with a blurred, dark background. He then shifts his gaze to the left as the frame cuts to a man with short grey hair and glasses, wearing a dark jacket and a light blue collared shirt, also in a similar studio setting with a blurred background. The words "LESSIG 2016" are repeatedly displayed in the background of these two frames, along with "lessig2016.us" in the top right. Next, the man with short grey hair and glasses, now wearing a light blue striped collared shirt, is shown speaking in profile against a warm-toned, dimly lit indoor background, with "lessig2016.us" in the top right. This is followed by a shot of him, dressed in a black long-sleeved shirt, standing in front of an audience in a wood-paneled room, speaking with his hands clasped as "LESSIG 2016" again appears repeatedly in the background. The scene then shifts to Edward Snowden, wearing glasses and a dark shirt, smiling and waving during a video call interface (showing "Google+" and a chat window), with "LESSIG 2016" again repeated in the background. Finally, the video ends with a close-up shot of Edward Snowden, still wearing glasses and a dark shirt, speaking directly to the camera in an indoor setting, with "LESSIG 2016" and "lessig2016.us" visible in the background.

A middle-aged man with receding gray hair and round glasses is shown from the chest up, wearing a light blue striped collared shirt. He is looking slightly to his left and appears to be speaking, with an engaged expression. The background is dark and out of focus, and in the top right corner, the text "lessig2016.us" is displayed.

The video opens with a split-screen effect, showcasing a segment from what appears to be a talk show. On the right, a man in a dark suit and glasses (Stephen Colbert) speaks animatedly, pointing his finger and gesturing with his hands, emphasizing his words. Opposite him, on the left, another man in a black shirt and glasses (Lawrence Lessig) listens intently, then begins to speak, gesturing calmly with his hands. The setting is a studio with a dark, reddish-toned background featuring stained-glass-like patterns and stylized American flag shields. A dark circular table sits between them, with a blue mug near Lessig and what looks like a book next to Colbert. Text on the screen reads "LESSIG 2016" repeatedly in the background and "lessig2016.us" in the top right corner. The scene then transitions to an outdoor protest in an urban environment, where a diverse crowd of people, bundled in winter coats, hold up various signs. Visible signs include "STOP PIPA," "It's no longer OK to NOT know how the Internet works. STOP PIPA," and "SAVE NY TECH STOP PIPA." These signs refer to the "Protect IP Act," a controversial piece of legislation. The crowd appears serious and engaged in the protest, with buildings and what looks like a railing or barrier visible in the background. The "LESSIG 2016" and "lessig2016.us" text persists throughout these scenes.

The video opens with a middle-aged man, with short, graying hair and glasses, wearing a light blue striped shirt, speaking directly to the camera against a blurry, dark brown background. The text "lessig2016.us" is visible in the top right corner. He then lowers his gaze and looks down and to his left, appearing contemplative. The scene transitions to a different man, bearded and wearing a gray knitted sweater, smiling faintly and looking off-camera to his right, with a blurry figure of another person in the background. This is followed by a close-up of a laptop screen displaying the Wikipedia logo—a globe made of puzzle pieces—and the text "WIKIPEDIA The Free Encyclopedia." The video then cuts back to the first man, who is once again speaking and looking slightly to his right, with the "lessig2016.us" text consistently present in the top right corner.

The video features a series of alternating shots of two main individuals, often interspersed with other scenes. It begins with a young man with dark, wavy hair and a beard, wearing a black t-shirt, sitting cross-legged on the wooden floor of a dimly lit bookstore, looking at the camera with a slight smile. This is followed by an older man with short, grey hair and glasses, wearing a light blue collared shirt, speaking to the side against a blurred brown background. The scene transitions to a TED talk stage where the older man, now in a white shirt and dark vest, speaks beside a laptop, while a large screen behind him displays a green field with the text "all the land below". The audience at the TED talk is shown laughing and smiling. Subsequently, the older man and the young man are seen sitting on an outdoor stone bench, facing each other and talking, with the older man holding a clear plastic cup. The video briefly displays the year "2011" in white text on a dark background, with a small dot inside the first '0', which then changes to "2007" with two dots in the '0's. Throughout these segments, the text "lessig2016.us" is consistently visible in the top right corner of the screen, and a "LESSIG 2016" watermark also appears during the TED talk scene. The video concludes with close-up shots of the young man smiling broadly, revealing his teeth, and the older man speaking.

The video segment opens with a dynamic display of three websites: "Stanford CIS" (The Center for Internet and Society at Stanford Law School) on the top left, featuring text like "WHISTLEE SURVEILL SERIOUS"; the "ELECTRONIC FRONTIER FOUNDATION" on the middle right, with a prominent banner reading "Tell Congress: Stop Mass Surveillance" (overlaid with a National Security Agency seal); and "creative commons" on the bottom, highlighting "SCHOOL OF OPEN LAUNCHES." This transitions to a photograph of a young, smiling Aaron Swartz (around 14 years old, according to the narration) wearing a grey "Creative Commons" t-shirt, standing beside a smiling Lawrence Lessig, who wears glasses and a dark jacket over a light blue shirt. Lessig is then shown alone, in a close-up, wearing a light blue striped shirt and glasses, looking contemplatively to the side against a blurred, warm background. The scene shifts to an older Aaron Swartz, with dark, shoulder-length hair and glasses, speaking into a microphone with a focused expression, wearing a black t-shirt with "DEMOCRACY NOW!" text, while sitting in front of a silver laptop in a dimly lit setting. This is followed by a shot of Aaron in a red "DEMOCRACY NOW!" t-shirt, outdoors, engaged in conversation with another man whose back is to the camera, with Aaron making a gestural movement with his hands near his ear. The narration explains that "Aaron Swartz committed suicide on Friday. He hanged himself in his Brooklyn apartment. He was 26 years old." The video concludes with Lawrence Lessig, wearing a dark vest over a light blue shirt and glasses, speaking directly to the camera with a serious and impassioned expression against a blue background adorned with repeated "HARVARD UNIVERSITY" text, remarking on the government's relentless pursuit of Aaron and the perceived disparity in justice compared to those responsible for the financial crisis.

The video segment begins with a young man wearing glasses, a black t-shirt with "Democracy Now!" printed on it, and a yellow lanyard, speaking animatedly while sitting in front of a laptop against a dark background (0:00-0:14). The background of the entire video features repeating "LESSIG 2016" and "lessig2016.us" watermarks. The scene then transitions to an older man with graying hair and glasses, wearing a light blue striped shirt, speaking with a serious expression, looking slightly to the left in a warmly lit indoor setting (0:14-0:22). Next, an animated map of New Hampshire appears, with "DIXVILLE NOTCH" at the top and "NASHUA" at the bottom connected by a black line, indicating a route. Vermont and Maine are also labeled, along with the Atlantic Ocean (0:22-0:30). This is followed by a wide shot of a group of people, dressed in winter gear including bright red, white, and yellow jackets, walking along a snowy, winding road next to a mountain range with bare trees under a clear blue sky (0:30-0:34). The video concludes with the older man from the earlier shot, still speaking with a focused expression (0:34-0:40).

The video opens with a close-up of an elderly woman with short gray hair, wearing a straw hat with a colorful band, looking upward with a slight smile; "LESSIG2016.us" is visible in the top right. This transitions to a shot of a person in a green shirt, orange safety vest, and cap, walking away with a staff on an uphill road surrounded by green foliage. A double exposure briefly overlays the elderly woman's face onto the walking figure, followed by a close-up of her face looking down, then a shot of a white patch on an orange vest reading "GRANNY D FOR CAMPAIGN FINANCE REFORM". The scene changes to a wide view of a snowy road with a Pizza Hut sign, where several people are walking along the shoulder, including one in a yellow safety vest. Then, a man in a red jacket and dark pants, using walking poles, approaches the camera on a snowy roadside, followed by another person. The Pizza Hut sign is shown again against a mountainous backdrop. Subsequently, a person in an orange safety vest is seen walking with a sign that partially reads "Corrupts Elections" with a dollar sign. The segment concludes with two people, one in a yellow safety vest and another in an orange safety vest holding a sign that reads "A BUCK IS NOT A VOTE", walking and smiling on a path beside a snowy road.

The video segment opens with a snowy, outdoor scene where a man in a blue jacket and dark beanie walks, overlaid with the large white text "96%." This quickly transitions to another snowy, flooded street scene featuring a "Road Closed" sign and two individuals, one in a yellow high-visibility jacket, with the "96%" text still present. The next shot shows two men in a TV studio, with the man on the left, wearing a black turtleneck shirt, gesturing while speaking to the man on the right, who wears a dark suit and tie, against a backdrop of a world map on a screen. The video then cuts to a medium close-up of the man from the TV studio, now wearing a light blue collared shirt and glasses, speaking directly to the camera with subtle hand gestures in a warmly lit indoor setting. Throughout the clip, "LESSIG 2016" is visible as a repetitive watermark, and the website "LESSIG2016.US" is displayed in the top right corner.

The video opens with a medium shot of a middle-aged man with light brown hair, wearing glasses and a light blue striped button-down shirt. He is speaking, looking slightly to the right of the camera with an earnest expression, occasionally glancing down. The background is a blurred, warm brown color. In the top right corner, the text "lessig2016.us" is displayed. At the 0:17 mark, the scene abruptly cuts to an exterior shot of a large, ornate building, likely in a city, with multiple American flags hanging from its facade. One particularly large American flag is prominently draped down the center of the building's front. Other tall buildings can be seen on either side. The text "lessig2016.us" remains in the top right corner, and a distinct beeping sound is heard as the scene changes.

The video opens with an upward shot of an American flag waving against a bright sky, with the Washington Monument and a plane contrail visible, and the text "lessig2016.us" displayed in the top right corner. A man in a light blue striped shirt and glasses is then shown speaking, followed by a series of environmental and economic imagery: an industrial site with smokestacks polluting an orange sunset, a power plant with three smokestacks emitting white smoke, a digital stock ticker displaying "YAHOO" and "Exxon" information, a "WALL ST" street sign, and the New York Stock Exchange building draped with American flags. The video then shows the Lincoln Memorial with numerous visitors and the U.S. Capitol Building under a blue sky, before returning to the man speaking about issues like "fundamental inequality," "political power," "dangers of climate change," "debts," "instability of our economy," and "the failure of social security," concluding that they are "all tied to the same issue" and "tied to this corrupt" (the sentence is cut off). The text "lessig2016.us" remains visible in the top right throughout the segment.

The video opens with a middle-aged man with short grey hair and round glasses, wearing a light blue striped shirt, speaking and gesturing with his right hand, against a warm brown background, with "lessig2016.us" displayed at the top right. The scene transitions to the same man, now in a black shirt, on a TV screen during what appears to be an interview with Stephen Colbert, surrounded by the repeated "lessig2016.us" text. This is followed by an aerial shot of a large assembly inside a grand, ornate chamber, likely the US Congress, with many people in attendance. The video then cuts back to the man in the light blue striped shirt, speaking against the warm brown background. Next, a close-up shows the gold lettering "NEW YORK STOCK EXCHANGE" carved above classical columns. The man in the striped shirt is shown speaking again, before transitioning to a TV studio where he, now in a dark suit and tie, is being interviewed by Chris Hayes, with a screen behind them displaying "LESSIG FOR PRESIDENT" and the channel's live broadcast information. This is followed by a busy daytime street scene with many pedestrians, then a nighttime protest with people holding signs and a large banner that reads "BLACK LIVES MATTER." The video returns to the man in the striped shirt speaking once more. Finally, a white screen appears with the text "IT'S TIME TO ACT" and "lessigforpresident.com," which then transitions to a logo featuring a blue and red flag-like symbol, "LESSIG 2016," "FIX DEMOCRACY FIRST," and "Paid for by Lessig Equal Citizens Exploratory Committee."
